sentences.en: A US perspective on the development of the frozen food industry
sentences.zh: 从美国的视角看冷冻食品行业的发展。

sentences.en: At some point in history, humans discovered that ice preserved food.
sentences.zh: 在历史上的某个时候，人类发现冰能让食物保鲜。

sentences.en: There is evidence that winter ice was stored to preserve food in the summer as far back as 10,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，早在一万年前，人们就会把冬天的冰储存起来，留到夏天用于保存食物。

sentences.en: Two thousand years ago, the inhabitants of South America’s Andean mountains had a unique means of conserving potatoes for later consumption.
sentences.zh: 两千年前，南美安第斯山区的居民就有一种独特的方法保存马铃薯，以供日后食用。

sentences.en: They froze them overnight, then trampled them to squeeze out the moisture, then dried them in the sun.
sentences.zh: 他们先把马铃薯冻上一夜，再用脚踩，挤出水分，最后放在太阳下晒干。

sentences.en: This preserved their nutritional value—if not their aesthetic appeal.
sentences.zh: 这样做保住了马铃薯的营养价值，至于卖相，就未必保得住了。

sentences.en: Natural ice remained the main form of refrigeration until late in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪后期，天然冰仍是冷藏的主要手段。

sentences.en: In the early 1800s, ship owners from Boston, USA, had enormous blocks of Arctic ice towed all over the Atlantic for the purpose of food preservation.
sentences.zh: 19世纪初，美国波士顿的船主让人把大块北极冰拖运到大西洋各处，用于保存食物。

sentences.en: In 1851, railroads first began putting blocks of ice in insulated rail cars to send butter from Ogdensburg, New York, to Boston.
sentences.zh: 1851年，铁路公司首次开始把冰块放进隔热车厢，将黄油从纽约州的奥格登斯堡运往波士顿。

sentences.en: Finally, in 1870, Australian inventors found a way to make ‘mechanical ice’.
sentences.zh: 终于，到了1870年，澳大利亚发明家找到了制造“机制冰”的办法。

sentences.en: They used a compressor to force a gas—ammonia at first and later Freon—through a condenser.
sentences.zh: 他们用压缩机把气体压过冷凝器，最初用的是氨，后来改用氟利昂。

sentences.en: The compressed gas gave up some of its heat as it moved through the condenser.
sentences.zh: 压缩后的气体流经冷凝器时，释放出一部分热量。

sentences.en: Then the gas was released quickly into a low-pressure evaporator coil where it became liquid and cold.
sentences.zh: 然后，气体被迅速释放进低压蒸发盘管，在里面变成液体，温度也降了下来。

sentences.en: Air was blown over the evaporator coil and then this cooled air passed into an insulated compartment, lowering its temperature to freezing point.
sentences.zh: 空气被吹过蒸发盘管，冷却后的空气再进入隔热舱，将舱内温度降到冰点。

sentences.en: Initially, this process was invented to keep Australian beer cool even in hot weather.
sentences.zh: 这项工艺最初是为了让澳大利亚的啤酒即使在炎热的天气里也能保持凉爽。

sentences.en: But Australian cattlemen were quick to realize that, if they could put this new invention on a ship, they could export meat across the oceans.
sentences.zh: 不过，澳大利亚的养牛人很快就意识到，如果能把这项新发明装上船，他们就可以将肉类销往大洋彼岸。

sentences.en: In 1880, a shipment of Australian beef and mutton was sent, frozen, to England.
sentences.zh: 1880年，一批冷冻的澳大利亚牛肉和羊肉被运往英格兰。

sentences.en: While the food frozen this way was still palatable, there was some deterioration.
sentences.zh: 用这种方法冷冻的食物虽然仍然可口，品质却有所下降。

sentences.en: During the freezing process, crystals formed within the cells of the food, and when the ice expanded and the cells burst, this spoilt the flavor and texture of the food.
sentences.zh: 在冷冻过程中，冰晶会在食物的细胞内形成。冰膨胀、细胞破裂时，食物的风味和口感就会受到破坏。

sentences.en: The modern frozen food industry began with the indigenous Inuit people of Canada.
sentences.zh: 现代冷冻食品工业的源头可以追溯到加拿大的原住民因纽特人。

sentences.en: In 1912, a biology student in Massachusetts, USA, named Clarence Birdseye, ran out of money and went to Labrador in Canada to trap and trade furs.
sentences.zh: 1912年，美国马萨诸塞州一名叫克拉伦斯·伯德赛的生物学学生花光了钱，于是前往加拿大的拉布拉多捕猎毛皮动物、做毛皮生意。

sentences.en: While he was there, he became fascinated with how the Inuit would quickly freeze fish in the Arctic air.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他对因纽特人借北极寒冷的空气迅速冻鱼的方法着了迷。

sentences.en: The fish looked and tasted fresh even months later.
sentences.zh: 即使过了几个月，这些鱼看起来、吃起来仍然很新鲜。

sentences.en: Birdseye returned to the USA in 1917 and began developing mechanical freezers capable of quick-freezing food.
sentences.zh: 伯德赛于1917年回到美国，开始研制能快速冷冻食物的机械冷冻设备。

sentences.en: Birdseye methodically kept inventing better freezers and gradually built a business selling frozen fish from Gloucester, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 伯德赛有条不紊地持续研制更好的冷冻设备，并逐渐在马萨诸塞州的格洛斯特做起了向外销售冻鱼的生意。

sentences.en: In 1929, his business was sold and became General Foods, but he stayed with the company as director of research, and his division continued to innovate.
sentences.zh: 1929年，他的企业被出售，成为通用食品公司。他留在公司担任研究主管，所领导的部门继续推陈出新。

sentences.en: Birdseye was responsible for several key innovations that made the frozen food industry possible.
sentences.zh: 伯德赛推出了几项关键创新，冷冻食品工业由此得以发展起来。

sentences.en: He developed quick-freezing techniques that reduced the damage that crystals caused, as well as the technique of freezing the product in the package it was to be sold in.
sentences.zh: 他开发了能减轻冰晶损害的速冻技术，还发明了让产品直接在销售包装中冷冻的技术。

sentences.en: He also introduced the use of cellophane, the first transparent material for food packaging, which allowed consumers to see the quality of the product.
sentences.zh: 他还引入了玻璃纸。这是首种用于食品包装的透明材料，消费者可以透过它看到产品的成色。

sentences.en: Birdseye products also came in convenient size packages that could be prepared with a minimum of effort.
sentences.zh: 伯德赛的产品所用包装大小合宜，准备起来也极为省力。

sentences.en: But there were still obstacles.
sentences.zh: 不过，仍然存在一些障碍。

sentences.en: In the 1930s, few grocery stores could afford to buy freezers for a market that wasn’t established yet.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代，冷冻食品市场尚未成形，很少有杂货店有能力为它购置冷柜。

sentences.en: So, Birdseye leased inexpensive freezer cases to them.
sentences.zh: 于是，伯德赛把价格低廉的冷冻陈列柜租给了这些店铺。

sentences.en: He also leased insulated railroad cars so that he could ship his products nationwide.
sentences.zh: 他还租用了隔热铁路车厢，以便把产品运往全国各地。

sentences.en: However, few consumers had freezers large enough or efficient enough to take advantage of the products.
sentences.zh: 然而，家里的冷冻柜足够大或效能足够好、因而能用上这些产品的消费者寥寥无几。

sentences.en: Sales increased in the early 1940s, when World War II gave a boost to the frozen food industry because tin was being used for munitions.
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代初，冷冻食品销量上升。第二次世界大战推动了这个行业的发展，因为当时锡被用于制造军火。

sentences.en: Canned foods were rationed to save tin for the war effort, while frozen foods were abundant and cheap.
sentences.zh: 为了把锡省下来供战争所需，罐头食品实行配给，冷冻食品则供应充足又便宜。

sentences.en: Finally, by the 1950s, refrigerator technology had developed far enough to make these appliances affordable for the average family.
sentences.zh: 终于，到了20世纪50年代，冰箱技术的发展使普通家庭也买得起冰箱了。

sentences.en: By 1953, 33 million US families owned a refrigerator, and manufacturers were gradually increasing the size of the freezer compartments in them.
sentences.zh: 到1953年，美国有3300万户家庭拥有冰箱，制造商也在逐渐增大冰箱冷冻室的容积。

sentences.en: 1950s families were also looking for convenience at mealtimes, so the moment was right for the arrival of the ‘TV Dinner’.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代的家庭还追求用餐方便，“电视晚餐”问世的时机由此成熟。

sentences.en: Swanson Foods was a large, nationally recognized producer of canned and frozen poultry.
sentences.zh: 斯旺森食品公司是全美知名的大型罐装和冷冻禽肉生产商。

sentences.en: In 1954, the company adapted some of Birdseye’s freezing techniques, and with the help of a clever name and a huge advertising budget, it launched the first ‘TV Dinner’.
sentences.zh: 1954年，这家公司对伯德赛的一些冷冻技术作了调整，凭借一个巧妙的名字和巨额广告预算，推出了首款“电视晚餐”。

sentences.en: This consisted of frozen turkey, potatoes and vegetables served in the same segmented aluminum tray that was used by airlines.
sentences.zh: 这份套餐有冷冻火鸡肉、马铃薯和蔬菜，盛放它们的是航空公司也在用的那种分格铝餐盘。

sentences.en: The product was an instant success.
sentences.zh: 这款产品一推出就获得了成功。

sentences.en: Within a year, Swanson had sold 13 million TV dinners.
sentences.zh: 一年之内，斯旺森公司就卖出了1300万份电视晚餐。

sentences.en: American consumers couldn’t resist the combination of a trusted brand name, a single-serving package and the convenience of a meal that could be ready after only 25 minutes in a hot oven.
sentences.zh: 一个值得信赖的品牌、一人份的包装，再加上放进热烤箱只需25分钟就能吃上饭的便利性，这样的组合让美国消费者难以抗拒。

sentences.en: By 1959, Americans were spending $2.7 billion annually on frozen foods, and half a billion of that was spent on ready-prepared meals such as the TV Dinner.
sentences.zh: 到1959年，美国人每年在冷冻食品上花费27亿美元，其中有5亿美元花在了电视晚餐等预制餐食上。

sentences.en: Today, the US frozen food industry has a turnover of over $67 billion annually, with $26.6 billion of that sold to consumers for home consumption.
sentences.zh: 如今，美国冷冻食品行业的年营业额超过670亿美元，其中有266亿美元来自销售给消费者在家食用的产品。

sentences.en: The remaining $40 billion in frozen food sales come through restaurants, cafeterias, hospitals and schools, and that represents a third of the total food service sales.
sentences.zh: 其余400亿美元的冷冻食品销售额来自餐馆、自助食堂、医院和学校，占餐饮服务业总销售额的三分之一。
